item.title: #3586619: Hide context items and usage records from JSON:API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586619 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

In AI Context (CCC) 1.0.0, context items and usage records are no longer available through core JSON:API. Before, a site that enabled JSON:API let every account with Use Published AI Context in AI Features page through all published context items over HTTP and read their raw fields, without the CCC delivery rules and without usage being recorded. Sites that read or synced items through JSON:API (for example with Entity Share) lose that access, and 1.0.0 has no supported replacement. Run drush cr after updating, because the resources stay available until caches are rebuilt. Core REST can still be enabled on purpose for context items, but no longer offers usage records. If you enabled a REST resource for usage records, delete it before rebuilding the router.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Removes a bulk JSON:API read path that let any account with Use Published AI Context in AI Features page through all published context items with raw fields, bypassing CCC delivery rules.
  • Config change: A site that enabled a core REST resource for usage records must delete rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage before drush cr or drush updatedb, or the router rebuild fails.

Technical details

ai_context_usage now has internal = TRUE in its @ContentEntityType annotation, so JSON:API, core REST discovery and other integrations that skip internal entity types ignore it. A side effect noted in the release note is that Workspaces now ignores usage records, so usage is also recorded while a non-default workspace is active.

ai_context_item is deliberately not marked internal, because Content Moderation and Workspaces skip internal entity types and the flag would remove the editorial workflow and moderation transition access checks. Instead, a new @internal subscriber, AiContextJsonApiResourceTypeSubscriber (registered as ai_context.jsonapi_resource_type_subscriber), listens to the string event name jsonapi.resource_type.build at priority 1000 and calls disableResourceType() for resource types whose name starts with ai_context_item--. Using the string event name means it works when JSON:API is not installed. No post-update is added; drush cr rebuilds the container, entity type definitions and JSON:API resource types.

A kernel test, AiContextEntityExposureTest, checks that with JSON:API enabled both resource types are internal and the user type is not, and that items keep the moderation handler. Docs changed in access-boundaries.md (new "Generic entity APIs" section and updated permission titles), api-stability.md (output of generic entity APIs such as core REST or the serializer is not public API; the scope field section is renamed "normalized shape") and configuration.md. The issue plans an opt-in for context items later (#3586600), which would need a dedicated read permission (#3586357).

Upgrade

After updating, rebuild caches so the container and JSON:API resource types pick up the change:

drush cr

If the site enabled a core REST resource for usage records, delete it first, before drush cr or drush updatedb, and remove it from config sync:

drush config:delete rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage

Also remove rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage.yml from the config sync directory. Otherwise the router rebuild fails because the REST plugin for usage records no longer exists.

  • Opened: October 18, 2026

  • pravesh_poonia (OpenSense Labs)

item.title: #3586489: Remove stale consumer config when a host entity is deleted
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586489 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

Deleting an AI Automator now removes its automator:{id} row from ai_context.consumers. Before this, only deleting an ai_agent did that, and a deleted automator showed up as a stale entry in the consumers listing until an admin removed it by hand. Consumer types from other modules can now get the same cleanup by declaring which entity type hosts them. A consumer type that fails to load is now skipped and logged instead of breaking entity deletes, the consumers listing, or routing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AiContextConsumerTypeInterface gains a required method; plugins that implement the interface directly instead of extending AiContextConsumerTypeBase must add it.
  • New API: AiContextConsumerTypeInterface::getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity() and a host_entity_type key on the AiContextConsumerType attribute.

Technical details

ai_context_entity_delete() no longer special-cases ai_agent. It calls a new AiContextConsumerTypeManager::getConsumerIdsForDeletedEntity(), which is marked @internal. That method asks every discovered consumer type plugin, including disabled or unavailable ones, because a leftover row can exist after a kill switch. Each returned ID goes to the existing AiContextScopeCleanupService::removeDeletedConsumerConfig(), so there is no second write path.

Each type answers through the new getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity(EntityInterface $entity): ?AiContextConsumerId method. AiContextConsumerTypeBase implements the 1:1 case from the new host_entity_type attribute argument. If the entity type matches and the ID is non-empty, it returns {plugin_id}:{entity_id}. Otherwise it returns NULL. The agent and automator plugins set host_entity_type to ai_agent and ai_automator. Types with a different ID scheme override the method. Types with no host omit the key.

AiContextConsumerTypeManager::getConsumerTypePlugins() now catches \Exception (not \Error) from createInstance(). It logs the failure and omits that type. The same applies to the mapping call. This is why a broken type is also dropped from the listing and from routing. The manager takes a new optional $logger argument, wired to @logger.channel.ai_context in ai_context.services.yml. No config dependencies were added on ai_context.consumers, and rows that are already stale are not cleaned up retroactively.

Upgrade

Plugins that extend AiContextConsumerTypeBase need no change. A type whose instances are 1:1 with a host entity can opt in through the attribute:

#[AiContextConsumerType(
  id: 'automator',
  // label and description omitted
  host_entity_type: 'ai_automator',
)]

Types with a different ID scheme should override getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity(). Do not gate it on isEnabled() or isAvailable(). Return NULL when the type does not own the entity.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 5, 2026

item.title: #3586470: Fix CCC beta4-to-beta5 upgrade and config-import path
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586470 · 1 contributor · 34 comments

Summary

Fixes three problems for sites upgrading AI Context from beta4 to beta5. Migrated agents now keep beta4's implicit Minimal selection mode instead of silently becoming Relevant. match_all becomes Broad, and explicit Minimal, Relevant and Broad values are preserved. A complete beta4 config export can be imported after updatedb. Its agents are turned into consumers, and the usage View is repaired. Settings without a selection mode fall back to the beta5 default. The one-shot post-update 0006 now removes only scope values whose entities no longer exist. Values for disabled or unavailable scopes stay. The beta5 release notes say to run drush updatedb before importing configuration, and to re-export afterwards.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: A beta4 ai_context.settings object without selection_mode is accepted on import, and a beta4 sync directory is converted to consumers during import.

Technical details

Update 10028 and the import transform share a new @internal helper, AiContextLegacyAgentConverter. convertAgentRow() normalizes the selection mode: missing or unrecognized becomes minimal, match_all becomes broad, valid modes are preserved. convertAgentsToConsumerRows() collapses identical duplicate rows and throws on conflicting duplicates. It also throws when the agents list is missing, because that is treated as corrupt rather than empty. Converted rows are written in the ai_context.consumers schema key order. Without that, StorageComparer would report a phantom update on every later import.

AiContextConfigImportValidateSubscriber now also subscribes to ConfigEvents::STORAGE_TRANSFORM_IMPORT via onImportStorageTransform(). When the source has ai_context.agents but no ai_context.consumers, it converts the rows and drops the leftover agents object. Per the issue it also does these things:

  • It supplies the agent consumer-type settings and copies the active Roles settings when the source omits them.
  • It remaps leftover usage-View handlers, beta1/beta2 paths and scope-map plugin IDs in place.
  • It runs the same residual repairs when ai_context.agents.yml is missing but structural leftovers remain, so a mixed sync does not delete beta5 settings or restore a leftover View.
  • It fails validation if leftover agents appear alongside consumers, and tells the site to re-export.
  • It is registered after Config Split's default merge and before Config Ignore.

ai_context_post_update_0006_scrub_stale_scope_values() now calls ai_context.scope_cleanup's scrubStaleScopeValuesForUpgrade(). This is a conservative upgrade-specific policy: it skips disabled or unavailable scope plugins, and removes Entity Types values only when the entity type or bundle no longer exists. It does not remove Site Section values based on pre-import settings, and it preserves Language values when Language is unavailable. The live settings-save cleanup from #3586416 is unchanged. The docblock of post-update 0004 now describes Relevant as the new-install default and Minimal as beta4's implicit behavior.

Upgrade

Run drush updatedb before importing configuration. A beta4 sync directory can still be imported after the upgrade, but re-export afterwards. Scope values for a language removed from active configuration, or for an entity type whose module is disabled in the database, are removed even if the incoming configuration re-adds them. Re-add those by hand after the import.

item.title: #3586466: Consumer include/exclude config stores context item entity IDs instead of UUIDs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: ersion::v1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586466 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

AI Context consumer "Always include" and "Never include" overrides are now stored as context item UUIDs instead of local numeric entity IDs. Before, exporting config and importing it into another environment could attach the wrong context item, or none, because the numeric IDs differed between databases. The exported ai_context.consumers.yml now also lists the referenced items under dependencies.content (for example ai_context_item:ai_context_item:<uuid>), so config import can use Drupal's missing-content dependency workflow. A post-update converts existing sites, so run database updates and re-export config.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: Post-update 0008 converts numeric IDs in ai_context.consumers to UUIDs and backfills dependencies.content.
  • Config change: ai_context.consumers always_include/never_include now hold context item UUIDs, with a new optional dependencies.content key.

Technical details

Config now stores UUIDs, while runtime selection still works with local entity IDs. AiContextSelectionFactory resolves stored identifiers (UUIDs or leftover numeric IDs) to local IDs when building an AiContextSelection, and AiContextSubscriptionBudgetCalculator does the same. The shared logic is in the @internal AiContextItemIdentifierResolverTrait. Input order is kept and the first occurrence wins. AiContextSelector::select() called directly still accepts UUIDs or numeric IDs. AiContextConsumerStoredConfig and AiContextConsumerResolvedConfig return the stored values as-is, so callers may see UUIDs or leftover numeric IDs.

AiContextConsumerForm saves UUIDs, still recognizes leftover numeric IDs when showing inclusion state (never wins over always, including mixed UUID and numeric entries), and rewrites them to UUIDs on save. On save it computes dependencies.content from getConfigDependencyName() of the referenced items and merges it into the existing dependencies map, so other keys such as module survive. An empty list removes only content. The previous carry-over of entries for deleted items was removed, so unknown identifiers are no longer dropped on save. The ai_context.consumers schema gains an optional dependencies key of type config_dependencies, and the always_include and never_include labels now say UUIDs. The GetRelevantAiContextItems function call parameter is relabeled "Always include UUIDs" and accepts UUIDs or leftover numeric IDs.

Post-update ai_context_post_update_0008_convert_consumer_context_item_ids_to_uuids() converts numeric IDs to UUIDs where the item still exists, deduplicates the lists, and backfills dependencies.content. Numeric IDs for items that no longer exist stay in the list. Per the issue, leftover ai_context.agents config is not converted and still holds IDs.

Upgrade

Run database updates (drush updb) so post-update 0008 converts stored numeric IDs to UUIDs and adds dependencies.content, then re-export config. Custom code that builds always_include or never_include lists can pass either UUIDs or numeric IDs; numeric IDs remain accepted until the next consumer form save or post-update.

item.title: #3586545: Store Tag and Taxonomy scope values as entity UUIDs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Critical task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586545 · 1 contributor · 22 comments

Summary

In AI Context, the Context Tags and Taxonomy Terms scopes now store the term's UUID instead of its serial term ID. Before this, default content and recipes could not carry these scope values across installs. Terms got new IDs on import, so items and consumer subscriptions pointed at the wrong term or at nothing. Recipes can now ship scope_id: tag with a UUID value, and the term YAML no longer needs a pinned tid. A post-update converts existing stored IDs. Unknown or deleted IDs are left as they are and stay unmatched.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_context_post_update_0013_convert_tag_taxonomy_scope_values_to_uuids rewrites tids to UUIDs in the item scope field tables, the scope index and consumer scope_subscriptions config.
  • Config change: scope_subscriptions for tag and taxonomy in ai_context.consumers and ai_context.agents now hold term UUIDs.
  • API change: AiContextItem::getContextTagIds() is removed. Tag and Taxonomy scope value IDs, in scope_subscriptions and item scope values, are now term UUIDs instead of numeric tids.

Technical details

Runtime matching was already string equality on scope.value, so the change is in what gets stored and how it is resolved. The new AiContextTaxonomyTermUuidTrait is used by AiContextScopeTag and AiContextScopeTaxonomy. It loads terms by stored value and converts autocomplete term IDs to UUIDs on save. getValues() keys options by UUID. Form defaults, label lookup, cacheable-metadata dependencies, stale-value detection and delete cleanup (getStaleTermValuesForEntityDelete()) all resolve by UUID. AiContextScopeTaxonomy also adds the taxonomy_term_list cache tag, because a stored UUID can start resolving after its term is imported. Detected request-entity values and getMatchingIndexedValues() now use term UUIDs.

Tag stale-value detection still keeps a leftover numeric tid until the post-update converts it, provided its tag is still offered.

ai_context_post_update_0013_convert_tag_taxonomy_scope_values_to_uuids() collects numeric values from ai_context_item__scope, ai_context_item_revision__scope, the scope index table, and scope_subscriptions in ai_context.consumers and ai_context.agents. It maps each tid to a UUID per scope: terms in the tags vocabulary map to tag, and all other terms map to taxonomy. A tid that points at the other scope's vocabulary is left for stale cleanup. The update rewrites the field tables, the index (dropping rows that would collide on the primary key) and the consumer config. It can be re-run if it stops partway.

AiContextItem::getContextTagIds() is removed. Callers can use getScopeValues('tag'), which the removed method wrapped. The scope diff builder, docs and AiContextSelection examples were updated to UUIDs. New test fixtures for a tagged item and a portable tag term cover the default-content round trip.

Upgrade

Run database updates so ai_context_post_update_0013_convert_tag_taxonomy_scope_values_to_uuids converts stored tids.

Custom code, recipes and exported config that pass serial term IDs for the tag or taxonomy scopes need to pass the term UUID instead:

scope:
  - scope_id: tag
    value: 7a1e8432-3616-438e-a411-76c93afba733

Term YAML in recipes should no longer set tid. Replace calls to the removed AiContextItem::getContextTagIds() with getScopeValues('tag'), which now returns UUIDs.

Contribution

item.title: #3586639: Status badge contrast (WCAG 1.4.3): Unavailable fails on row hover
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586639 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

The status badges in the AI Context listing and on the item page no longer change contrast when the row behind them is hovered or striped. An accessibility audit found the Unavailable badge dropped to 4.23:1 on row hover, below the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum of 4.5:1. With the fix it measures about 4.53:1 in every row state, in light and dark mode, by the issue's own calculation. The Disabled badge still fails AA on its own (about 4.18:1 before any hover). That comes from Gin's danger colours and was left for an upstream Gin issue.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Status badge CSS in css/ai_context.css and css/ai_context_item.css now sets background-color and background-image instead of the background shorthand; themes overriding the badge background may need to adjust.

Technical details

The badge colours come from Gin variables such as --gin-status-warning-bg, which are semi-transparent. Gin's row hover tint therefore showed through and lowered contrast. Changing CCC's literal fallback values would have had no effect on a Gin site, since Gin defines the variables. The fix keeps Gin's palette and gives each badge an opaque base instead. The base class sets background-color: var(--gin-bg-layer, #fff). Each status modifier then paints its colour with background-image: linear-gradient(var(--gin-status-*-bg, …), var(--gin-status-*-bg, …)). A gradient is used because background-image can layer a flat colour over the opaque base colour. --gin-bg-layer follows the theme, so it covers dark mode too. The change applies to .ai-context-status* in css/ai_context.css and to .ai-context-item-entity__status* in css/ai_context_item.css. Text colours are unchanged.

item.title: #3586541: Make duplicate consumer_id rows resolve consistently and map validator errors to the right row
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586541 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

If a duplicated consumer_id row gets into ai_context.consumers (through drush config:set, custom code, or a database edit, since the UI cannot create one), AI Context now treats the first row as the real one everywhere. Before, the consumers listing showed the last row while runtime used the first, so the listing could show push off while content was still pushed. Saving any consumer no longer fails because of an unrelated duplicate. The editor drops the later repeats and shows a warning. Removing a consumer now deletes every row with that ID.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The first row wins in the consumers listing (AiContextConsumersForm), runtime resolution, the consumer editor and the validator message. This matches AiContextSelectionFactory::loadConsumerConfig() and update 10028, which already used the first match.

AiContextConsumerConfigValidator reports the duplicate violation on the later row. The message now reads Duplicate consumer ID "%s". Row %s already uses it and is the row that takes effect. A third repeat is measured against the first row.

AiContextConsumerForm removes later repeats from the whole consumer list on save, keeping each ID's first row. After a successful save it logs a warning to the ai_context channel and shows a status warning naming the de-duplicated IDs. A second save shows no warning. The remove form deletes every row with the ID, following AiContextScopeCleanupService::removeConfigListRow(). docs/developers/consumer_api.md now documents that consumer_id is unique, which row wins, de-duplication on save, and full removal.

A non-duplicate violation on an unrelated row, such as max_tokens below the schema minimum, still blocks every consumer save. The issue lists this as out of scope. I read the merged code in the repo but did not have a diff for this issue.

Contribution

  • Opened: September 19, 2026

item.title: #3586571: Scheduled publish on save can leave context item Draft in the listing
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586571 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

On a moderated site with Scheduler enabled, saving an AI Context Item whose Publish on date was already due used to publish the item but leave its moderation state at Draft. The listing showed Draft while selection and counts treated the item as published. The moderation state now follows the scheduled publish state, so the listing shows Published. Future dates handled by cron already worked and are unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Scheduler publishes immediately in hook_entity_presave() when the date is due and dispatches SchedulerAiContextItemEvents::PUBLISH_IMMEDIATELY. scheduler_content_moderation_integration only listens to the node and media versions of that event, so moderation_state was never updated. The listing reads moderation_state, while selection and counts use the status flag.

The fix adds an @internal event subscriber, AiContextSchedulerImmediatePublishSubscriber, registered as ai_context.scheduler_immediate_publish_subscriber. It takes content_moderation.moderation_information as an optional dependency, so it does nothing when Content Moderation or Scheduler is absent. On the event it checks that the entity is moderated, has the publish_state field, and that the field is not empty. It then copies publish_state into moderation_state. Like the node and media handling, it leaves publish_state in place. Cron publish and unpublish go through the generic Scheduler hooks and were not changed. A kernel test (AiContextSchedulerImmediatePublishTest) covers a due publish_on without SQL backdating.

item.title: #3586638: Scope settings table: Edit links do not say which scope they are for (WCAG 2.4.4)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586638 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

On the AI Context Scope settings page, all the Edit links were just called "Edit", so screen reader users could not tell which scope each one opened. Each link now has an accessible name that includes the scope, such as "Edit Global", while the visible text stays "Edit". The scope name in the first column is now a row header, so assistive technology announces it as the heading for its row. This addresses WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.4 (Link Purpose) and SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships).

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Scope overview table now renders the first cell of each row as <th scope="row"> and Edit links carry an aria-label.

Technical details

The change is in src/Form/AiContextScopeOverviewForm.php. The label cell gets '#wrapper_attributes' => ['header' => TRUE, 'scope' => 'row'], so the table element renders a th instead of a td. Each operations link gets 'attributes' => ['aria-label' => $this->t('Edit @scope', ['@scope' => $plugin->getLabel()])]. The label starts with "Edit", so voice control users can still say "Edit" (SC 2.5.3 Label in Name). The issue also lists a functional test checking that each Edit link has its own name and that the first cell is a th with scope="row". I read the form code in the repo but did not read the test.

item.title: #3594686: Failure-mode taxonomy artifact for error analysis
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594686 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval module now has failure modes: named categories such as "hallucinated_fact" that reviewers use to group the problems they find in open-coding notes. Failure modes are managed under Failure Modes in the AI Eval admin area and can be exported and imported as a shareable, versioned taxonomy. Reviewers can tag an annotation with a failure mode. The UI can then report how often each mode occurs, including an untagged bucket, so the dominant failure modes are visible.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New ai_eval.failure_mode.* config entities with keys id, label, description, taxonomy_id, weight, status.
  • New API: New ai_eval_failure_mode config entity, FailureModeTaxonomySerializer and FailureTaxonomyValidator services, FailureRateService, and schema/failure_taxonomy.schema.json.

Technical details

FailureMode is a config entity (ai_eval_failure_mode, config prefix failure_mode). It is managed at /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/failure-modes and exports id, label, description, taxonomy_id, weight and status. Modes sharing a taxonomy_id (default default) form one taxonomy. The issue proposed a suggested check or judge prompt seed field, but the entity as it stands has no such field.

schema/failure_taxonomy.schema.json is a peer to the dataset schema. It requires id, version (semver) and modes. Each mode needs id, label and description, with an optional integer weight, and unknown mode properties are rejected. FailureModeTaxonomySerializer::export() produces that shape. Its import upserts modes and never deletes modes missing from the payload. FailureTaxonomyValidator checks a serialized taxonomy against the schema using opis CompliantValidator, in the same way as DatasetValidator.

The ai_eval_annotation entity gets a failure_mode entity reference field. FailureRateService groups annotation rows with a single GROUP BY on the base table. It provides rates per eval result (ratesForResult()) and per target with an optional time window (ratesForTarget()), and a variant over reviewed conversations. Rate is the per-mode count divided by all annotations in scope, and untagged annotations are always included so rates sum to 1.0. This work was merged across several commits, and the trace review linkage landed under #3594752. The repository history has no single commit for this issue, so this summary is based on the final code.

item.title: #3594690: Artifact source plugins expose capabilities for read/write/promote/versioning
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594690 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval dataset sources (file, config, entity) now say what they can do. File and config sources are read-only. The entity source can also be written to and can take promoted traces and annotations. Writing and promotion go only to sources that support them, and existing file-based datasets keep working as before. The issue's wider capability list (listable, versioned, remote, validates_schema) is not in the code I read. Neither is a capability-driven source picker.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Custom dataset source plugins must provide capabilities(). Extending DatasetSourceBase gives them ['read'] by default.
  • New API: DatasetSourceInterface::capabilities() returns capability tokens (read, write, promote), and a new WritableDatasetSourceInterface adds appendQuestions() and createDataset().

Technical details

The change was found by reading the current ai_eval main branch, not a fix diff, because the issue had no linked diff and no comments. The code comments reference #3586840 and #3594690.

DatasetSourceInterface declares capabilities(): array, which always contains read. DatasetSourceBase implements it as ['read'], so FileSource and ConfigSource inherit read-only. EntitySource returns ['read', 'write', 'promote'].

Write support is a separate WritableDatasetSourceInterface, which extends DatasetSourceInterface. It adds appendQuestions(string $ref, array $questions) and createDataset(string $label, string $origin = 'manual'). appendQuestions() validates every question against the dataset JSON Schema before persisting anything, and it persists none if any question fails. The interface docs say to use instanceof WritableDatasetSourceInterface for type safety and capabilities() for UI introspection.

In the code I read, the enforcement paths PromotionService::writableSource(), GenerationRunner and GenerationController::isWritableDataset() check instanceof WritableDatasetSourceInterface, not capabilities(). WritableSeamTest::testWriteCapabilityMatrix checks that only entity advertises write and that write implies the interface. I did not verify that any UI code calls capabilities().

Upgrade

item.title: #3594780: Apply decision calibrations to the callers a site selects
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594780 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval gets an optional submodule, AI Eval Decision Calibration. Until now only the decision rubric judge used a calibration, and other callers such as the "Decision: Boolean" automator got the raw probability. With the submodule, a site picks which callers use an active calibration, and only those callers get the corrected probability. The issue's own test numbers show why this is scoped: a curve fitted on another model's answers made calibration error worse. A site can also record a sample of a caller's true/false answers, have people review them, and fit a curve from those reviews. The Callers tab then warns if the curve does worse than the raw probability on answers recorded after the fit.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New ai_eval_decision_calibration module with a scope third-party setting on calibrations and record settings (callers and sample rate).
  • Permission change: No new permissions. The Record decisions page needs administer ai eval, and the Callers, Review and Fit pages need validate ai eval judges.
  • New API: New CalibrationFingerprint::fromDecision(), hook_ai_eval_calibration_view_alter(), and an optional $thirdPartySettings argument on CalibrationStoreInterface::save().

Technical details

The new ai_eval_decision_calibration module requires ai_eval and ai, and Drupal ^11.3. Its CalibrationSubscriber listens to PostGenerateResponseEvent at priority 10, so the AI module's validation subscriber (priority 20) runs first. For the decision operation it handles each NoulAnswer. It computes the fingerprint with the new CalibrationFingerprint::fromDecision(), which also accepts array instructions and NULL criteria. It looks up the active curve through CalibrationStore::fresh() using the provider, the model that answered (DecisionResponse::getModel()) and that fingerprint. The curve applies only if its scope third-party setting (request tags such as ai_automator:id:<id>) intersects the event tags. An empty model ID or an empty scope means no correction. Score and choice answers are untouched. A matching answer is rebuilt with the calibrated probability, and its raw data gets an ai_eval_calibration entry with raw_probability, calibration and tag. If anything fails, the output stays unchanged and a warning is logged.

Calibration scope is stored as a third-party setting on EvalCalibration. CalibrationStoreInterface::save() gets an optional $thirdPartySettings argument. When a new active curve replaces an active one, it inherits the old curve's third-party settings unless it sets its own. A new hook_ai_eval_calibration_view_alter() lets modules change the calibration detail page. The submodule uses it to replace the judge-use text for scoped calibrations.

DecisionRecorder stores sampled true/false answers. A row holds the entity reference, field name, question wording, provider, answering model, raw probability and any applied calibration. It does not store the state sent to the model. Answers are skipped when the response reports no model, or when the question wording contains text from the state. Recorded answers are deleted when their entity is deleted. New admin forms cover choosing callers, record settings, blind review and fitting from recorded decisions (RecordedFitForm). Fitting needs at least 30 reviewed answers, both classes on the fitted side, and held-out answers, with answers about one entity kept on the same side of the split. A fit that worsens the held-out Brier score is saved inactive. The calibration is not deactivated automatically when it later does worse. The Callers tab shows a warning.

Upgrade

Enable the module, open a calibration from Manage > Calibrations, then its Callers tab. Select the automators that should use it. To build a curve from a caller's own answers, use Record decisions, Review decisions, then Fit a calibration > From recorded decisions. Modules that call CalibrationStoreInterface::save() need no change, because the new $thirdPartySettings argument is optional.

item.title: #3594747: Workflow target mode: a pipeline as the system under test (v0 slice)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594747 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

ai_eval (1.1.x line) can now test a whole workflow, not only an AI agent or a chat model. A target set to mode: workflow runs a pipeline from a workflow engine such as FlowDrop. The pipeline can have deterministic steps, tool calls, model calls and nested sub-workflows. The response text is graded by the existing graders, and the steps taken are stored with each question's result. ai_eval depends on no engine: a bridge module supplies the engine. This first slice has no target form and no step tree view, so workflow targets are created as config YAML. With no engine runner installed, a workflow target is refused at run time with a message naming the missing engine.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: EvalTarget gains optional workflow_engine, workflow_id, workflow_input_port, workflow_inputs, workflow_output_path and workflow_snapshot keys, exported only when mode is workflow.
  • New API: New Drupal\ai_eval\Workflow\WorkflowRunnerInterface (id(), listWorkflows(), inputPorts(), run()), value objects WorkflowRunResult, WorkflowStep, ModelCall, WorkflowRunOptions, WorkflowLaunchRefusedException, and the ai_eval.workflow_runners collector for services tagged ai_eval.workflow_runner.

Technical details

An engine implements WorkflowRunnerInterface and registers it as a service tagged ai_eval.workflow_runner. WorkflowRunnerCollector (service ai_eval.workflow_runners) indexes runners by id(). It throws a LogicException on a duplicate engine id or a tagged service that does not implement the interface. Because tagged services are lazy, this check happens on first read, not at container build. run() is synchronous and returns a WorkflowRunResult. Anything knowable before work starts (unknown workflow, malformed inputs) must be thrown as WorkflowLaunchRefusedException, so a record can tell "never ran" from "ran and failed". Runners must not retry on ai_eval's behalf.

In EvalRunner, mode dispatch is now an explicit match, with a workflow arm calling invokeWorkflow(). It builds inputs from the target's fixed workflow_inputs, merges the question's metadata.inputs, and sets the question text on workflow_input_port. A fixed input on the question port is refused. Each question's scores_json gets a bounded workflow block, written on graded rows and on failed or refused rows. The block holds steps, model calls, status and failure kind. A WorkflowStep has an engine-assigned kind from a closed set (ai, tool, deterministic, subflow, other). Steps form a tree by execution id, with an optional free-text engineKind and capped input and output previews. The handoff doc gives the v0 budgets as 200 steps, 500-character previews and a 64 KB block. I did not verify these in code. token_usage is the run total. The new workflow_* keys on EvalTarget are added to config_export, toRunnerConfig() and the config schema. Existing agent and chat targets export unchanged. A user guide section was added in docs/user/usage/targets.md.

Upgrade

A bridge module registers its runner like this (the tag name is from ai_eval.services.yml; the service and class names are placeholders):

services:
  my_bridge.workflow_runner:
    class: Drupal\my_bridge\MyWorkflowRunner
    tags:
      - { name: ai_eval.workflow_runner }

A target then references it by engine id:

mode: workflow
workflow_engine: flowdrop
workflow_id: summarize_v2
workflow_input_port: url

This is a proposal (MR !22), not yet merged. If it lands, installing or updating drupal/ai_best_practices will write a small docs/ai/PROJECT.md into the project. The file lists the Drupal version, PHP version, local environment (DDEV or Lando), the DDEV URL, and a count of custom-module directories. The plugin also adds a # This project section to AGENTS.md. That section only says when an agent should load PROJECT.md, so the file is read on demand and not at session start. Removing the package deletes the generated files and the injected block. The issue started as a much larger harvest of services, hooks and entity bundles. After review that part was dropped from this MR.

Affects module maintainers.

The MR adds src/Harvester/ContextHarvester.php. AiBestPracticesPlugin calls run() after ComposerProjectSynchronizer::runDeferredSyncIfPending() and calls cleanup() from uninstall(). Both calls are wrapped in catch (\Throwable) and only emit a <warning>, so a failure never makes Composer exit non-zero.

run() first checks that composer.json requires a drupal/core* package. It then reads composer.json (package name, drupal/core or drupal/core-recommended constraint, PHP constraint) and the filesystem. A .ddev/ directory gives a <name>.ddev.site URL, taken from .ddev/config.yaml or the directory name. A .lando.yml file is detected as Lando with no URL. Custom modules are counted as the directories under <web-root>/modules/custom. The web root comes from extra.drupal-scaffold.locations.web-root, with fallbacks web, docroot, public_html and htdocs.

The AGENTS.md block sits between the HTML comment markers MARKER and MARKER_END. A rerun replaces the existing block in place. If the end marker is missing, everything from the start marker to the end of the file is stripped and a fresh block is appended. cleanup() removes the block and also deletes the legacy PROJECT_MODULES.md, PROJECT_SERVICES.md, PROJECT_HOOKS.md and PROJECT_ENTITIES.md names, which earlier iterations of the branch produced.

It adds a README section and eval fixtures under evals/. The drupal-project-context eval fixture and its SKILL.md still contain the full services, hooks and entities content that this MR no longer generates. The eval runner gains a file_contains check and a php_lint_wrapper option.

No action is needed until it merges. If it does, docs/ai/PROJECT.md will be generated on each composer install or composer update. Whether to commit it is still open: the README suggests committing it so composer install --no-dev environments have it.

item.title: #3586558: Preserve HTML in streamed output (1.3.x)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586558 · 1 contributor · 33 comments

Summary

Streamed AI responses that contain HTML no longer get stray closing tags injected mid-sentence. The reported case was AI Translate in the GUI, where text such as <strong>…</strong> in a page body came back split into extra <p> paragraphs and sentences were broken apart. Streamed output now keeps the HTML the model produced.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

StreamedChatMessageIterator buffers streamed chunks and flushes them through HostnameFilter::filterText(). In HTML mode the filter parses the text as a fragment and re-serializes it. When a flush landed mid-element, for example after an opening <strong> but before its closing tag had streamed, the HTML5 parser auto-closed the open tags and dropped the orphaned closing tags. That corrupted the markup.

shouldFlush() now returns FALSE while a new private helper, bufferHasUnclosedHtml(), reports that the buffer is unbalanced. The helper returns TRUE when the buffer ends inside an unfinished <… tag, or when a stack-based scan of the tags finds non-void, non-self-closed elements still open. Whatever remains is flushed at end of stream, where the full message is balanced. Two guards limit the hold. A new constant MAX_HTML_BUFFER_SIZE (102400 bytes) forces a flush if a tag never closes, so malformed output cannot grow the buffer without bound. The hold is also skipped while a streaming guardrail is registered ($streamingGuardrailStates non-empty), because guardrails do their own start/stop buffering and holding the buffer across their markers would change what they evaluate. The commit adds a unit test, StreamedHtmlIntegrityTest, that re-chunks HTML at several sizes and checks that it round-trips unchanged.

Claude Code only loads project skills from .claude/skills/, but ai_best_practices synced skills into .agents/skills/ by default, so Claude Code users got no skills unless they changed the setting by hand. item.title: #3583083: Entity input violation tells an in-process invoker that it cannot pass entities
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583083 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

When a non-entity value (such as a node ID) was set on an entity input, Tool told every invoker without the entity handle capability that it "cannot pass entities". That was false for in-process invokers like ECA, which hand real entity objects to tools. The validation message now states only the reason, "This input must be an entity.", for every invoker. drush tool:run still gives its own advice to use a tool that takes an entity type and ID.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New TypedInputsInterface::NOT_AN_ENTITY_ERROR violation code, set on the violation for a non-entity value on an entity input.

Technical details

The first fix attempt, from #3583046, keyed the hint on InvokerCapability::EntitiesAsHandles. That capability only says whether an invoker uses handle strings. It does not say whether the invoker can carry a PHP object. The fix drops the invoker check from TypedInputsTrait. Validation cannot know what an invoker can supply, because any module may turn what an invoker sent into an entity through an input transform. The violation is now always This input must be an entity. and carries the new code TypedInputsInterface::NOT_AN_ENTITY_ERROR.

An invoker that knows its own boundary can match on that code and add its own advice instead of matching on the message. ToolRunCommand does this. When a failed run, not an access denial, has a violation with that code, it appends drush tool:run cannot pass entities; use a tool that takes an entity type and ID instead. The check covers list items and map properties too. Tests cover the message and code with no invoker, a capability-less invoker and a handles invoker, and check that the code survives the path rebuild for list items. They also check that Drush adds the advice only for entity violations.

item.title: #3583108: Check view label access before including an entity label in handle hints and Drush output
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583108 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Tool no longer shows an entity's label to an account that is not allowed to see it. Before, the label: line of a handle hint and the label in drush tool:run output could reveal, for example, the title of another author's unpublished node to a user with only "access content". Now the label is shown only when core's view label check passes, and is otherwise omitted (NULL).

  • Security: Information disclosure: labels (such as the title of an unpublished node) of entities the account cannot view were shown in handle hints and Drush tool:run output.

EntityHandleTransformer::getAccessibleLabel() now first requires $entity->access('view label', $account). Where the entity type has a label field, it also still requires field view access on it. Entity types without a label field, such as user, get only the entity check. The new optional $account defaults to the current user. Handle hints are built while the tool runner has switched to the run-as account, so they omit it.

Drush prints after the runner has switched back from the --uid account, so a plain check there would use the wrong user. The formatOutputValue() and referenceEntities() methods moved from ToolOutputTrait into ToolRunCommand and now take the run-as account. ToolRunCommand gets EntityHandleTransformer (tool.entity_handle_transformer) injected through its constructor. Content entities go through getAccessibleLabel($value, $account). Config entities, which have no field access, use a bare view label check, which the code comment says matches the JSON:API split. item.title: #3583005: Advertise truthful formats for unmarked datetimes and timestamps
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583005 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

Tool input schemas now describe what Drupal actually accepts. Timestamp inputs advertise integer seconds as well as RFC 3339 strings, so strict clients such as the MCP bridge, which validates arguments against the schema, no longer reject a bare integer. Datetime inputs with no date-only or date-time marker advertise both a full date-time and a bare date, instead of core's date-only date. Output schemas are not changed. If you have clients or tests that depend on the old advertised schema, expect the output of schema normalization to differ.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Advertised input JSON schema changes: core-path timestamp inputs become type: ["string","integer"] (plus null if optional); unmarked datetime_iso8601 inputs advertise anyOf of date-time and date formats.

Technical details

The change is in InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer (src/Normalizer/InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer.php). The issue text proposed advertising plain format: "date-time" for unmarked datetimes. The committed code differs: for an unmarked datetime_iso8601 input, it removes format and emits anyOf: [{format: date-time}, {format: date}], with the description note "An RFC 3339 date-time, or a date alone as YYYY-MM-DD." The comments in the code give the reason: the input coercion subscriber re-emits a full datetime in canonical form but leaves a bare Y-m-d date untouched, and naming only date-time would make a strict invoker reject the bare date. Marked definitions are unchanged: DateOnly gives date, DateTime gives date-time.

For timestamp on the core (11.1+) path, an input schema of type: string is widened to ["string", "integer"]. The note becomes "An RFC 3339 date-time or a Unix timestamp in seconds." This is skipped for OutputDefinitionInterface objects, because the output transform sends the string core describes. The legacy path already used integer and keeps its Unix-seconds note. The optional-input handling now also appends null to an array-valued type, so a union gains the null branch the same way a single string type does. Unmarked datetime outputs are deliberately left alone, since the output transform only rewrites to RFC 3339 under the DateTime marker. The commit also updates the schema matrix and acceptance tests.
